requirement_paraphrase: Recommends not relying only on GNSS, cross-checking with other navigation sources, assessing interference likelihood on planned and diversion routes and having backup plans.

instrument: CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 harmonised standards (EN 18286 and drafts)
edition_or_version: EN 18286 (QMS for AI Act); prEN 18228, 18229, 18282, 18284 etc. drafts
status_note: Same. The official page says 'In June'; the Modulos 12 July date is unsupported officially.
requirement_paraphrase: CEN-CENELEC says EN 18286 was approved and the Commission is expected to cite it in the OJ later in 2026. Secondary pages say risk management (prEN 18228), cybersecurity (18282), dataset quality (18284) and trustworthiness framework (18229) remained drafts.
applies_to: Providers seeking presumption of conformity under AI Act Art. 40

requirement_paraphrase: Certificate of conformity requires test reports from accredited laboratories covering 17 items: general design requirements, electrical safety, vibration/shock, EMC, GPS feature, safe fall/return/hovering, noise, MTOM, max altitude, range/endurance, horizontal speed, transmission power, geographical boundary identification, frequency compatibility, total flight time, response to government anti-drone interception systems, and collision-avoidance technology.
applies_to: Manufacturers/importers seeking a UAE conformity certificate

requirement_paraphrase: Article 12 makes Annex A standards binding for certification. Annex A lists ISO (e.g. ISO 21384-2/-3, ISO 23629-8:2023 remote ID), SAE AS 6513A, ASTM (F3298-19, F2910-14, F3116, F3227, F3231, F3411-22a) and IEC 61508, IEC 62133, IEC 62368-1.
applies_to: Applicants for UAE drone conformity certificate

instrument: Cabinet Resolution No. (110) of 2023 on the UAE scheme for drone products and systems
edition_or_version: Issued 6 Nov 2023 (22 Rabi II 1445) per portal
status_note: In force day after publication; 180-day transition for importers/manufacturers
requirement_paraphrase: Before importing, selling, assembling, manufacturing or operating a drone: approval from GCAA/competent authority, a conformity certificate (renewed every three years) or a product status statement, serial-number statement card, Arabic/English warnings and safe-use manual, a data tracking/transmission system approved by the Cyber Security Council and regulator, approval before design modification or main-part repair, licensed spare parts.
applies_to: Manufacturers, importers, sales centres, owners and operators of civil drones in UAE incl. free zones

instrument: Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 129 final (standardisation request for Reg. 2023/1230), Annexes 1-2
clause_or_section_seen: Annex I Tables 1 and 2 (items 2, 3, 4, 5, 15, 16); Annex II
requirement_paraphrase: Asks CEN/CENELEC for standards on machinery with self-evolving behaviour or ML safety functions, protection of safety functions against corruption, autonomous mobile machinery, and robotics incl. collaborative and service robots. Deadlines: Phase 1 20 Jan 2026, Phase 2 20 Jan 2034.
applies_to: Standards bodies; shows expected future harmonised standards

instrument: Defeaters and Eliminative Argumentation in Assurance 2.0
requirement_paraphrase: Argues that assurance cases should record defeaters (doubts) and investigate them; a case is closed only with no unsupported claims and no active defeaters.

status_note: In force since 1 Jul 2019 per EUR-Lex metadata; entry into application of class rules per later amendments not checked
requirement_paraphrase: C0: MTOM under 250 g, max 19 m/s, 120 m height. C1: under 900 g or impact energy under 80 J, 19 m/s, 120 m; must have direct remote ID broadcast, geo-awareness, lost-link method, lights and low-battery warning, serial number per ANSI/CTA-2063.
applies_to: UAS placed on EU market for open category

status_note: In force since 1 Jul 2019 per EUR-Lex metadata; entry into application of class rules per later amendments not checked
requirement_paraphrase: C1 geo-awareness function must load airspace data, warn the pilot of potential breach, and (per extraction) flag when its positioning is unreliable.

status_note: In force since 1 Jul 2019 per EUR-Lex metadata; entry into application of class rules per later amendments not checked
requirement_paraphrase: Conformity assessment via internal production control, EU-type examination or full quality assurance; EU declaration of conformity; CE marking plus class label (at least 5 mm high) and sound power indication.

status_note: In force since 1 Jul 2019 per EUR-Lex metadata; entry into application of class rules per later amendments not checked
requirement_paraphrase: Art. 40: design, production and maintenance must be certified if the UAS has a characteristic dimension of 3 m or more and is designed for operation over assemblies of people, or is designed to carry people, or to carry dangerous goods requiring high robustness; or where a specific-category authorisation risk assessment finds the risk cannot be mitigated without certification. Art. 41: operators from third countries must follow Implementing Reg. 2019/947 in single European sky airspace; competent authority is that of the first Member State of operation.
applies_to: Certified-category UAS; non-EU operators flying in EU

edition_or_version: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026, OJ L series 24.7.2026
status_note: Entered into force 27 July 2026 (EUR-Lex metadata; Recital 46: third day after publication). OJ header shows 24.7.2026 next to the L reference but is not labelled as the publication date in the extraction.
clause_or_section_seen: Title and metadata only (EUR-Lex fetch gave metadata, not body)
requirement_paraphrase: Regulation amends Regulations 2024/1689 (AI Act), 2018/1139 (aviation safety) and 2023/1230 (machinery) as regards simplification of AI rules.
applies_to: EU AI Act stakeholders; machinery and aviation manufacturers

instrument: Dubai Executive Council Resolution No. (3) of 2019 (testing autonomous vehicles)
requirement_paraphrase: Testing requires an RTA contract and Authorisation; RTA sets safety standards for each test phase and designates roads and times; establishments file periodic stage reports and carry insurance.

instrument: Dubai Law No. (4) of 2020 regulating drone activity in Dubai
edition_or_version: Issued 2020; effective on Official Gazette publication per Media Office
status_note: Law summary page last updated 4 Jul 2020; implementing resolutions not retrieved
requirement_paraphrase: All drone-related operations in Dubai and its free zones require a Dubai Civil Aviation Authority licence; owners register drones with DCAA; operational safety certificate before flying; permits for drone infrastructure; privacy and recording limits; imprisonment/fines for violations.
applies_to: Drone operators, manufacturers, owners in Dubai

instrument: Dubai Law No. (9) of 2023 Regulating the Operation of Autonomous Vehicles
edition_or_version: Issued 6 Apr 2023; effect 90 days after publication (Art. 27)
status_note: In force; implemented by RTA resolutions
requirement_paraphrase: 'Vehicle' includes machines built to run on Roads; an AV may not travel on a Road unless RTA-licensed; a Permit is needed per Activity; licensing requires the RTA-prescribed technical inspection, conformity to UAE-approved specifications and UAE-licensed insurance; changes to the Autonomous Driving System or ODD need prior RTA approval; the Operator must immediately notify Competent Entities of any accident and provide data on request; the ADS must be capable of connecting to RTA-adopted systems; the Operator is liable for damage.
applies_to: AV operators and agents in Dubai (roads)
